articles.title: Sexual harassment row hits Indian shooting: SAI coach faces allegations
articles.summary: More sports News: A shooting coach, who travelled with the Indian team for the Junior World Championships in Suhl, Germany, in June, is in the dock after facing sexual .
articles.body: A shooting coach, who travelled with the Indian team for the Junior World Championships in Suhl, Germany, in June, is in the dock after facing sexual harassment allegations from junior rifle shooters who competed at the tournament.According to NRAI sources, the coach, an employee of the Sports Authority of India (SAI), appeared before the Internal Complaints Committee of the National Rifle Association of India earlier this week.“The committee heard his response to the allegations and, based on the report from the NRAI, the SAI has moved him out of the Dr Karni Singh Shooting Range in Tughlakabad,” an NRAI official told TOI.The coach, who was recruited nearly three years ago, allegedly misbehaved with the shooters during the championships.“The range is located on Friedberg Hill, on the outskirts of Suhl. The complaint is that the coach allegedly took the two shooters for a walk in the nearby woods and touched them inappropriately. Earlier, the coach even tried to get the charges dropped, threatening to ruin the careers of the shooters,” the source said. “One of the shooters’ parents had lodged an oral complaint after the incident, but nothing came of it.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Reitz football pull away in Week 3 win against Jasper
articles.summary: Reitz found success early and never looked back in its Week 3 win against Jasper. Here's how they secured a third-straight dominant victory.
articles.body:
See our best photos of Jasper against Reitz in high school football week 3

EVANSVILLE — After what initially looked like a close encounter was brewing between Jasper and Reitz, the latter pulled away and won in a blowout. Again.

It finished 56-21 at the Reitz Bowl on September 4.

For Jasper coach Derek Hart, his outlook was plain and simple.

"We got whooped," Hart said. "We talked all week about taking care of the football, and in the first drive of the game, we throw a pick. We struggled defensively, but we have to compete better than we did tonight."

This week's heat wave affected both teams' preparation for Week 3, but Hart would not use that as an excuse. His group got outplayed.

The pick Hart was referring to was a Jaxson Woodring interception early in the first quarter. It was one of two takeaways for the junior — the other being a scoop and score for a touchdown in the fourth quarter. Reitz had three turnovers altogether, as E'Ani Clardy caught an interception in the third quarter.

It was the second-consecutive week for Woodring to find the end zone defensively. He said it is a result of what his defense is doing through three weeks.

"I'm doing everything I can, but it's a team sport," Woodring said. "Defense is doing everything right, we just come ready to play."

It was another challenging quarterback for the Panthers to deal with in Week 3. Jasper's Jaylen Maners is an all-state quarterback with the ability to attack defenses through the air and on the ground. He put it all together as he willed the Wildcats down the field for a touchdown before halftime.

Still, Reitz made the plays needed to halt the Wildcats on multiple possessions. Panthers coach Cory Brunson was pleased with the effort.

"(Maners) still did a lot of good things that we have to get better in stopping," Brunson said. "But it was another team effort."

The Reitz offense impressed, surpassing the 40-point mark for the third week in a row.

Amyr Wilford will get the praise (two touchdowns vs Jasper) for what he brings to the field every week, and deservedly so. He had a minor scare Friday, though, when limped off the field in the second half. He did return shortly thereafter.

His fellow sophomore, quarterback Hunter Moers, has also been effective. Moers has been an efficient operator to open the season. Few balls are hitting the ground.

Moers finished the game with 4 touchdowns. Three went to Mason Bailey, who showcased his ability to separate and run after catch. The other went to Lee Steele on a trick play in the second quarter.

From the offensive line to the skill positions, Moers said everything seems to be meshing on offense. And through three weeks as the starter for Reitz, he is feeling well acclimated to the new role.

"It's going well," Moers said. "Just continuously watching film, working hard every day in practice and making sure I'm on with my guys."

In Week 4, the Panthers head to Bundrant Stadium to face North, who emerged from its Week 3 matchup at Harrison with a 22-20 win. Although the Huskies are 1-2, it remains a tough challenge to mitigate the threat Jayden Jones and Hunter McKinney bring as a quarterback/running back duo.

"We have to work hard at practice this week," Woodring said. "Take every day serious, and every rep. We'll see how it goes."

Brunson said North should be undefeated. He expects a tough test at Bundrant.

As for Jasper, a trip to Bosse awaits in Week 4. Hart hopes for a response from the Wildcats, as was the mentality heading into their Week 2 win against Harrison.

Markos Tsegaye is a sports reporter for the Courier & Press. He can be reached at mtsegaye@usatodayco.com. Follow him on X @10_Markos_.

articles.title: Marion Harding football gives coach the fast start he craved in Week 3 win
articles.summary: Marion Harding wanted to start fast in its first road trip of the football season and did just that at Bellefontaine on Sept. 4.
articles.body:
BELLEFONTAINE — C.J. Westler asked his team for it all week, and they delivered.

"Our goal all week was a fast start. I think we did that," he said.

Marion Harding scored on its first two possessions of the game, and the defense took care of the rest in a 14-7 road victory Sept. 4 at Bellefontaine in a Week 3 high school football game.

"We moved the ball a little bit in the second half, but we just couldn't finish drives," Westler said. "They kind of caught us off guard going tempo on that first drive (of the second half when Bellefontaine scored). They ran it right down the field.

"Our defense responded. We made a lot of mistakes, but they played extremely hard. We made a couple fourth-down stands down in the red zone."

It took just five plays and 1:22 off the clock to start the game with a 7-0 lead. Dez Feliciano hit Jaden Jordan for a 38-yard pass play and Jackson Payne for an 11-yard gain before striking with Reggie Walker for a 13-yard score.

On the next possession, it looked like Feliciano scored on a 97-yard keeper, bouncing off tackles down the field, but a holding call brought it back. Nevertheless, the Presidents engineered a 14-play drive that ate nearly six minutes off the clock. Feliciano earned that second touchdown on a 2-yard run.

"Our kids play extremely hard, but we told them last week that playing hard is not good enough. You don't want to be the team that says, 'Man they play hard, but they don't win,'" Westler said.

Bellefontaine opened the second half with an 11-play, 60-yard drive that Dillon Jones finished on a 1-yard run. That cut the Harding lead to 14-7, but that was the only blemish by the Prexy D.

In the first half, the Presidents stopped Bellefontaine on a fourth-and-goal from the 3, then on the next series stopped it again on fourth-and-goal from the 5. Payne picked off a pass to thwart a third drive.

In the second half after the BHS touchdown, Harding's defense posted back-to-back 3-and-outs, then stopped the hosts on a fourth-and-4 from the Harding 44. The defense put the game away when Sean Kelly recovered a fumble with 1:37 left.

"In years past, this is the kind of game we would have let slip away. I feel like we're finally starting to turn that corner to where we're able to weather the storm and be able to finish it off," Westler said.

Both teams finished with 13 first downs, but Harding outgained its opponent 351 to 232 in total yards.

Feliciano was 9-for-24 passing for 129 yards, plus ran it 16 times for 75 yards. McGary finished with 107 yards on 12 carries, and Shaukoyre Jackson ran eight times for 36 yards. Walker made four catches for 43 yards and Jordan three catches for 70. Quincy Carter paced the defense with 6.5 tackles, and Kolten Sibrel added 4.5. Noah Shockley and Maddox Moran shared a crucial sack in the second half.

articles.title: 3 biggest takeaways from Oklahoma's dominant win over UTEP
articles.summary: Three key takeaways from Oklahoma's dominant season-opening win over UTEP.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners kicked off the 2026 college football season with a dominant 51-0 win over the University of Texas at El Paso Miners. The Sooners dominated this one from start to finish, outscoring the Miners 21-0 in the first quarter.

While it was a great win to start the season, with both the offense and defense having their moments, it wasn't all perfect. Here are the three biggest takeaways from the Sooners' win on Friday.

The run game is heading in the right direction

This was one of the biggest topics of the offseason. The Sooners showed early that they wanted to focus on the run game. They tried it from all different looks, including under center. But the run game was more like death by a thousand cuts than a dominant showing. Oklahoma ran for 170 yards and two scores on 4.4 yards per carry, but only two runs topped over 20 yards. Lloyd Avant led the way with 79 yards on 15 carries.

The Sooners just consistently were eeking out four or five yards a carry. That's not bad, but it wasn't as dominant as it could have been. Now, it's important to point out: three projected starters on the offensive line missed most of the game. Center Jake Maikkula and guard Ryan Fodje both missed the game due to injury. Tackle Michael Fasusi played sparingly, likely wanting to make sure he stayed healthy.

The defense still has some things to clean up

The Sooners' defense on paper looked like it played a dominant game. It pitched a shutout and allowed less than 200 yards of total offense. The defense also forced two turnovers. But UTEP had some success. The Miners got into Oklahoma territory multiple times, but missed three field goals.

The biggest issue was missing tackles. The Sooners missed far too many tackles and gave up outside containment multiple times. Oklahoma allowed 112 yards on the ground, including a 51-yard run by Raymond Moore II. Quarterback EJ Colson Jr. also had some success, especially early in the game.

It was still a good performance, and you never want to be upset by a shutout. Oklahoma had four sacks and 10 tackles for loss. The Sooners led the nation in both stats last season. Still, it felt like the Sooners left a lot on the table that they will have to clean up before facing the Michigan Wolverines next weekend. Fans shouldn't be worried yet with Brent Venables at the helm.

The tight end room could be a real strength

If there was one position group that provided an especially encouraging glimpse of what's possible this season, it was the tight ends. The Sooners consistently ran 12 personnel on offense, meaning two tight ends. That was typically Hayden Hansen and Rocky Beers. They even went 14 personnel at one point. Jack Van Dorselaer and Trynae Washington played a role early.

On top of that, the tight ends played a role in the passing game. Beers had two catches for 43 yards and a touchdown. That includes his 40-yard touchdown. Hansen also had one catch for 15 yards in the game.

It's obviously important not to overreact to what happened against UTEP. The competition gets considerably tougher from here. But the way Oklahoma used its tight ends suggests this could be a much more involved position group than it was a year ago. And that's encouraging for an offense that is trying to become more physical while taking some pressure off quarterback John Mateer.

For an opener, Oklahoma got almost everything it needed from Friday night. Mateer completed 11-of-17 passes for 225 yards and three touchdowns, Isaiah Sategna delivered an 88-yard punt return for a score and the defense pitched a shutout.

Now comes the real test. Michigan will expose weaknesses that UTEP couldn't, particularly on the road and in the trenches. If Oklahoma can carry the physicality it showed Friday while eliminating the missed tackles and continuing to develop its rushing attack, the Sooners will enter Ann Arbor with considerably more confidence than they had a week ago.

articles.title: LSU leaves Dae'Quan Wright, Zxavian Harris off roster as SEC punishment threats linger
articles.summary: LSU will not roster NFL camp participants Zxavian Harris and Dae'Quan Wright as the SEC continues to battle in courts.
articles.body:
LSU is finding that the problem with a declawed cat is that it can still bare its teeth.

As the school continues to fight a protracted battle against the SEC that seems to be destined for the courts, the Tigers' roster for the season opener was reportedly missing a few notable names, per Pete Thamel: NFL camp participants Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, who were expected to be rostered after being granted a preliminary injunction by a Louisiana judge on Sept. 3. The SEC later issued a statement that it expects schools to follow its rules.

The move comes in the wake of the SEC threatening dramatic action against teams rostering players who were previously on NFL rosters, including:

50% of season suspension for head coaches

50% of that sport's annual operating budget

SEC voting privileges revoked on some matters

While it was initially reported the conference's charter members unanimously voted in approval of the punishments, it was later reported LSU abstained from the vote.

In an interesting twist, LSU only filled 103 of its 105 roster spots, leaving a path for Wright and Harris to be added at a later date.

Why were Zxavian Harris, Dae'Quan Wright left off LSU's roster?

Although the ruling from Judge William Jorden opened the door for LSU to roster Wright and Harris, there is a tremendous amount of scrutiny surrounding the two names.

LSU has been under heavy fire for considering carrying the two on its 105-man roster, and the SEC has promised steep punishments against teams trying to play players who were previously with NFL teams. In a move that preempted Jorden's ruling, the SEC filed suit against LSU and Lane Kiffin, claiming that its First Amendment rights were being violated by LSU playing the players at direct odds with SEC rules.

With that in mind, though the preliminary injunction prevents the NCAA, SEC, or LSU from taking action against the players, the threat of retribution from the SEC is still very real, and if LSU rosters Harris and Wright it runs the risk of retroactive punishment in all games they participate in. In other words, they're being left off until there's more clarity.

Can Dae'Quan Wright, Zxavian Harris be added to LSU roster later?

With two roster spots open, LSU is sending a clear message it wants Wright and Harris on the team. The two are enrolled at LSU, so they can be added later.

However, with the amount of uncertainty hanging in the air over this situation, LSU is clearly trying to slow-play it until it knows it can get away with having the two on the team. It's a half-measure, to be sure, but ultimately the door is very much open to add Wright and Harris later.

articles.title: Brighton vs Leeds United – Predicted lineup and team news
articles.summary: A first home game in three weeks brings a familiar opponent for Brighton, who have not lost to Leeds United at the Amex Stadium in over a decade.Fabian Hurze...
articles.body:
A first home game in three weeks brings a familiar opponent for Brighton, who have not lost to Leeds United at the Amex Stadium in over a decade.

Fabian Hurzeler's side will look to bounce back from their first defeat of the season, having been beaten 4-3 at Chelsea last time out. Hurzeler has praised Daniel Farke's Leeds as a "hardworking team" who "don't give away a lot of chances," and expects Saturday's game to be "a fight" despite his own side's attacking pedigree so far this season.

Jack Hinshelwood, Yankuba Minteh, Kaoru Mitoma, Mats Wieffer, Stefanos Tzimas and Evan Ferguson are all sidelined through injury, with Wieffer not expected back until after next month's international break. Georginio Rutter and Yasin Ayari are both doubts having missed the defeat at Chelsea, though Hurzeler sounded encouraged about Ayari's chances of involvement, saying of his ankle knock: "He could finish the game against Tromso, so hopefully it's not that bad."

Costinha could be handed his first start at right-back in Wieffer's absence, while new signings Chema Andres and Femi Azeez are both in contention to feature, most likely from the bench. Pascal Gross, who scored and set up a goal against Chelsea, continues in midfield and is closing in on 250 Premier League appearances. Charalampos Kostoulas remains an option up front should Rutter not be risked from the start.

Brighton & Hove Albion possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Verbruggen; Costinha, Vuskovic, Dunk, Kadioglu; Ayari, Yalcouye; Gomez, Gross, De Cuyper; Rutter

The Premier League match kicks off at 15:00 on Saturday, 5 September 2026.

The match falls under the traditional 3pm Saturday blackout and will not be shown live in the UK.

articles.title: Crystal Palace XI vs Fulham – Predicted lineup and team news
articles.summary: Crystal Palace will look to get their first win of the new Premier League season when they take on Fulham on Saturday at the Craven Cottage.Crystal Palace ar...
articles.body:
Crystal Palace will look to get their first win of the new Premier League season when they take on Fulham on Saturday at the Craven Cottage.

Crystal Palace are enduring a tough start under new manager Pierre Sage, as they are hunting for their first points. The Eagles opened their campaign with a 2–0 loss away to Everton before suffering a heavy 4–1 defeat at home to Manchester City. Defensively fragile, Palace have conceded six goals in two games. Their solitary goal so far this term came courtesy of an own goal, highlighting a critical lack of cutting edge up front.

Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage faces a far more challenging selection dilemma as he hunts for his first points of the new campaign with a heavily depleted squad.

The Eagles will be entirely without star striker Jean-Philippe Mateta, who has been ruled out for roughly three weeks after sustaining a hamstring injury.

Ismaïla Sarr is also sidelined with a groin issue, having missed recent training following a collapsed transfer move to Liverpool.

Furthermore, defender Chadi Riad remains sidelined long-term with a severe knee injury. On a brighter note, Sage could hand debuts to a wave of late transfer arrivals.

Ben Chilwell, Honest Ahanor, Quinten Timber, and Darío Osorio have all trained with the first team and are fully eligible to feature. Osorio, in particular, is heavily tipped to receive early minutes out wide to help offset Palace's attacking absences.

Possible Crystal Palace starting XI: Henderson; Canvot, Richards, Tomiyasu; Khalaili, Kamada, Wharton, Mitchell; McNeil, Larsen, Pino

The match will kick off at 3pm BST on Saturday, 5th September.

The match will not be telecast due to the 3pm blackout rule in the UK.

articles.title: Manchester City vs Coventry City – Match preview and team news
articles.summary: Manchester City can extend a perfect start to the season when they host newly promoted Coventry City at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday. Enzo Maresca’s side h...
articles.body:
Manchester City can extend a perfect start to the season when they host newly promoted Coventry City at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday.

Enzo Maresca's side have won both of their opening matches, while Frank Lampard's Coventry are yet to open their account for either points or goals.

This will be the two clubs' first meeting since March 2002, when City won 4-2 at Maine Road with both sides then in the second tier. Their history in the top flight is more competitive than Saturday's odds suggest, though: Coventry are unbeaten in their last eight Premier League meetings with City (W4 D4), a run stretching back to the 1992-93 season, when City won both fixtures.

Both sides overhauled their squads before Tuesday's transfer deadline: City completed a club-record £125m deal for Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea, while Coventry added eleven new signings across the summer as they returned to the top flight after 25 years away.

Manchester City vs Coventry City – Match preview and team news

Last meeting: Manchester City 4-2 Coventry City (Second Division, March 2002)

Jeremy Doku remains sidelined with a calf injury, but Matheus Nunes has recovered from a muscle problem and is available again. Enzo Maresca confirmed deadline-day signing Enzo Fernandez is ready to make his full debut, while fellow new arrival Iliman Ndiaye is also available for selection. Ayyoub Bouaddi, who impressed off the bench last time out, could be handed a first start.

Haji Wright remains a long-term absentee, while Sidiki Cherif is a doubt, though Frank Onyeka has recovered from a hip problem and is available. Bobby Thomas is expected to continue at centre-back having come off with cramp against Hull, with Frank Lampard considering a switch to a five-man defence. Ephron Mason-Clark is set to partner Taiwo Awoniyi in attack, though his involvement is subject to a final fitness check.

Manchester City have made the perfect start under new head coach Enzo Maresca, beating Bournemouth 2-1 before winning 4-1 at Crystal Palace, with Rayan Cherki and Erling Haaland scoring twice apiece. City also lead the Premier League for successful passes and passing accuracy so far this season, reflecting the possession-based approach Maresca has already instilled.

Coventry have lost both of their opening fixtures without scoring, beaten 3-0 by Arsenal before a narrow 1-0 home defeat to Hull City. It is a daunting start to their first top-flight campaign in 25 years, coming immediately after winning last season's Championship title, and Frank Lampard has stressed the need for his players to adjust their mindset.

Manchester City predicted XI (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Bouaddi; Foden, Cherki, Semenyo; Haaland

Coventry City predicted XI (5-3-2): Rushworth; Van Ewijk, Thomas, Pinnock, Amenda, Dasilva; Yirenkyi, Grimes, Onyeka; Mason-Clark, Awoniyi

Maresca has praised the impact of a busy transfer window, thanking the club's ownership after a summer of significant squad turnover. The head coach has stressed the need for focus despite City's status as overwhelming favourites, warning that games against promoted sides "can be tricky" if his side are not fully switched on.

Jeremy Doku remains sidelined with a calf injury sustained in the Community Shield defeat to Arsenal and has missed both of City's opening league fixtures. There is better news on Matheus Nunes, who has recovered from a muscle problem that forced him to sit out the win at Crystal Palace and is available for selection again.

Enzo Fernandez, City's £125m deadline-day signing from Chelsea, has been confirmed ready to make his full debut by Maresca, who called the Argentine "a winner" with "a winning mentality." Fellow new arrival Iliman Ndiaye is also in contention, though Maresca may opt to stick with Phil Foden and Antoine Semenyo in wide areas. Ayyoub Bouaddi, who made his debut off the bench against Palace, could be handed a first start alongside Elliot Anderson in central midfield.

articles.title: Extra Point, Week Two: Slocomb Red Tops hosts Booker T. Washington Golden Eagles
articles.summary: SLOCOMB, Ala. (WDHN)—The Slocomb Red Tops are on the hunt for their first win of the year, and hope to do so today when they face the Booker T. Washington Go...
articles.body:
SLOCOMB, Ala. ( WDHN )—The Slocomb Red Tops are on the hunt for their first win of the year, and hope to do so today when they face the Booker T. Washington Golden Eagles.

The last time these two teams met was back in 2023, when the Red Tops fell 43-6.

articles.title: Williams sisters exit US Open but excite - what does future hold?
articles.summary: Serena and Venus Williams may have lost in their US Open doubles return, but the veteran pair proved they can still compete on an entertaining night in New Y...
articles.body:
Rarely has a women's doubles first-round match headlined the US Open night session - but the Williams sisters are like no other pairing.

Serena and Venus Williams might have a combined age of 90, but their star remains undimmed. Neither does their ability to compete at the highest level when they are in tandem.

Even though the superstar siblings - aged 44 and 46 - lost on their highly-anticipated Grand Slam return, their performance in a narrow defeat by 14th seeds Hao-Ching Chan and Maya Joint led to an entertaining night in New York.

A packed Arthur Ashe Stadium roared on the American icons as they looked on course for a memorable win - but ultimately fell short in a 6-3 6-7 (6-8) 7-6 (10-7) loss.

"It was unbelievable how competitive that was," said former American player-turned-commentator Chanda Rubin, who lost to the Williams sisters in the 1999 US Open doubles final.

"After the first set you wondered if Serena and Venus would be able to find their mojo - but, boy, they did."

Four years after they last appeared on Ashe, the Williams sisters were given a rapturous reception as they strode onto a court where they have won eight singles titles between them and two doubles titles together.

The decibel levels were rarely matched in an underwhelming first set for the home favourites, but the noise quickly returned when they rallied in the second set.

The atmosphere became muted as the decider seemed to run away from them at 4-1 down, before they showed indomitable spirit - a hallmark of their extraordinary careers - to take their opponents into a first-to-10 match tie-break.

Racing into a 5-0 lead put the Williams sisters firmly on course to reach the second round, only for Chan and Joint to fight back - with the help of a double fault from each opponent.

Despite the initial despondency of the home fans, the volume was turned back up when the American pair were given a fond farewell - with everyone left wondering what the future holds for them both.

Serena hinted earlier this week she wanted to play singles again in an interview with Good Morning America, while Venus said after her singles exit on Monday that she should not "have to" think about her future beyond the doubles.

The questions about what happens next were not addressed by the pair following Friday's match. The sisters decided they were "not available" to speak to the media, US Open organisers said.

For once, the 20,000-odd fans on a packed Arthur Ashe Stadium sat quietly engrossed during points.

The sight of the Williams sisters back on court together at the US Open - possibly for the final time - commanded ultimate respect from a chatty crowd known to let their attention wander.

The siblings changed the face of the sport when they emerged as precocious teenagers in the 1990s, going on to dominate the sport with a combined 30 Grand Slam singles titles and 14 doubles victories as a pair.

Three decades later, the sport remains captivated by them.

Serena, a record 23-time Grand Slam women's singles champion, coming out of retirement this summer sparked excitement among those who saw them in their prime and those too young to have witnessed it.

Seven-time major winner Venus has never "evolved away" from the sport - the words chosen by her younger sister when she last played in 2022 - but instead continued her career with the help of sporadic wildcards.

While that has proved controversial in some quarters, there were few objections about the sisters being invited to play once again at Flushing Meadows.

Their planned return at Wimbledon was scuppered by the knee injury which Serena suffered in her singles match there - ironically a defeat by 20-year-old Joint - before they finally reunited at the WTA event in Cincinnati.

The comeback ended in a match tie-break defeat by Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk and her American partner Peyton Stearns, with the same fate befalling them in New York.

When the Williams sisters last played on Ashe four years ago, they suffered a straight-set defeat by Czech pair Lucie Hradecka and Linda Noskova in the first round.

It looked like being a similar fate as they meekly surrendered the first set against Chan and Joint, then batted off four break points in the fifth and seventh games of the second set.

But once Serena upped her level to match her impressive sister, they managed to switch the momentum back in their favour and level the match.

An absorbing contest featuring some sensational points saw the Americans fight back again in the decider, only to falter from a commanding lead in the tie-break.

Overall it was a more than credible performance from the veteran pair. Their solid groundstrokes, sharp movement and never-say-die attitude caused problems for their opponents, who deserve huge credit for staying focused in a partisan environment.

"The atmosphere was surreal," said Joint.

"It was something we've never experienced before, and to play against such legends of the game was super special."
authors: Jonathan Jurejko - BBC Sport tennis news reporter
